title: Keśi Tīrtha Upakaṇṭhe
author: Sanskrit composition by Śrīla Rūpa Goswāmī

text: mā prekṣiṣṭhās tava yadi sakhe bandhu-saṅge ’sti raṅgaḥ
translation: My dear friend, if you are indeed attached to your worldly friends, do not look at the smiling face of Lord Govinda as He stands on the bank of the Yamunā at Keśī Ghāṭa. Casting sidelong glances, He rests the tender blossoms of His lips upon His flute. His transcendental body, bending in three places, appears very bright in the moonlight.
*Corresponding Bengali composition by unknown composer, from the Maṭh’s Śrī Gauḍīya Gitāñjali*

text: tabe mora kathā rākha    yeyo nāka yeyo nāka
translation: If you have desire – if you have any desire – to laugh and enjoy in the company of friends, then remember my words: do not go, do not go, near the ghāṭ at Keśī Tīrtha in Mathurā!

text: kibā tri-bhaṅgima ṭhāma    varṇa samujjvala śyāma
translation: Bearing the figure of Govinda, Hari is present there with a side-long glance in His eyes and a mild smile on His face. What a threefold pose! His complexion is a radiant dark blue, and the beauty of His divine limbs resembles tender new leaves.

text: se mūrti nayane here    keha nāhi ghare phire
saṁsārī gṛhīra ye go haya sarva-nāśa
translation: The flute at His lips is the cause of disaster! O brother, no one can believe His peacock feather crest, and after seeing His figure with their own eyes, no one returns home! A family man and householder who does so meets with utter ruin.

text: ghaṭibe vipada bhāri    yeyo nāko he saṁsārī
translation: Thus I feel great fear in my mind that grave danger will befall you. So do not go, O family man, near the ghāṭ at Keśī Tīrtha in Mathurā!
